questions.q: Why is skepticism from a portfolio manager or risk officer treated as a normal part of the process rather than an attack?
options: Because it means the strategy will definitely be rejected
Because surviving hard questions is the same risk-management instinct that motivated purged walk-forward validation and honest cost modeling in the first place
Because research reports are never actually reviewed by anyone
Because skepticism only applies to strategies that failed their backtest
questions.explain: Skepticism in the room reflects the same culture that drove honest out-of-sample validation and cost modeling earlier in the project — it's a feature of good research practice, not hostility.

questions.q: What is the honest, complete answer to "how do I know this isn't overfit?"
options: It cannot be overfit because 18 years of data is enough to rule that out entirely
Purged walk-forward validation produced an out-of-sample Sharpe, which reduces overfitting risk, but 18 years is still one historical path and regime change remains a real risk
Overfitting is not a concern for dollar-neutral strategies
The question should be deflected rather than answered directly
questions.explain: The reported Sharpe is out-of-sample via purged walk-forward validation, which reduces but does not eliminate overfitting risk — a point worth stating plainly rather than overselling.

questions.q: During the COVID crash, why did SR-5's beta to SPY spike to roughly 0.25 despite being dollar-neutral?
options: The short leg was accidentally closed out during the crash
Dollar-neutral construction reduces net market exposure on average, not in every regime — when every sector sells off together, the long and short legs stop moving independently (correlation-to-one)
SPY itself became more volatile, which mechanically raises every strategy's beta
The Ridge regression model was retrained mid-crisis with different coefficients
questions.explain: Correlation-to-one describes how cross-sectional diversification breaks down in a panic, raising net market exposure even in a dollar-neutral book — exactly what happened in COVID.

questions.q: What is a 'kill criterion' in the context of defending SR-5 to a skeptical audience?
options: A rule for removing underperforming sector ETFs from the universe
A pre-defined condition, stated in advance, under which the live strategy would be shut down or re-researched
The threshold at which transaction costs exceed gross returns
A statistical test for removing outlier trading days
questions.explain: Kill criteria are conditions defined ahead of time — such as live Sharpe falling well below the net backtest figure of 0.42 — that would trigger stopping or re-researching the strategy.

questions.q: How should a researcher honestly answer a question about using free Stooq data instead of a paid institutional feed?
options: Insist the data is identical in quality to a paid vendor feed
Avoid the question since data sourcing isn't relevant to performance
State directly that Stooq is appropriate for this research exercise, but a live deployment would warrant revalidating against a paid, exchange-sourced feed first
Claim that data source never affects backtest results
questions.explain: Naming the real gap between free research-grade data and institutional-grade feeds — and what you'd do about it before trading real capital — builds credibility rather than eroding it.
